keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 1099 but the infobox gives "Established: 1098 (First Crusade)" and the crusaders entered Antioch on 2 June 1098. The shape is the city and its immediate surroundings; the 1099 shape (Antioch, Artah, the Orontes valley) grows from it.

7.6 k km2: Antioch, Artah, Harim, Baghras and the Saône district (gazetteer check: Antioch, Artah, Harim, Saône inside). "took full control of Antioch as well as of the surrounding places such as Artah". The page gives no area figure (only "roughly 20,000 inhabitants in the 12th century"), so no comparison. Tancred's regency (1100-1112) "seiz[ed] the cities of Tarsus and Latakia from the Byzantine Empire" without dates; Cliopatria never includes Latakia or Tarsus.

15.4 k km2 for 1111-1138: adds Atarib, Sarmin and Ma'arrat al-Numan, which "rapidly fell into Muslim hands" after Ager Sanguinis on 28 June 1119; "Baldwin recovered some of the lost towns" (unnamed). The shape is therefore the high-water mark: the ledger records the 1119 loss and the unnamed partial recovery. Cliopatria's 1111 step is not dated by any page opened (Tancred's regency, 1100-1112). Re-read 2026-10-25 (Tancred page): Latakia (April/May 1103, held by 1108) and Cilicia (conquered 1109-1111) are outside the shape; the page does not mention Atharib.

15.6 k km2 for 1139-1151, same land as 1111. 1138: John II Komnenos "arrived in Antioch in 1138 and forced Raymond of Poitiers to swear fealty" (Byzantine vassalage 1138-1153 in the infobox); no territorial change. Marked adjust after review: the shape is right to 1148 but "Much of the eastern part of the Principality was lost ... at the battle of Inab in 1149" (Principality page), so 1149-1151 follow the ledger.

correction.text: the 1169 shape without Harim, held from 1164 (valid 1164-1176; Cliopatria draws the step in 1169)

keyframe_review.note: 7.9 k km2 for 1177-1187: no grid cell differs from the 1169 shape (gazetteer check), so the step is a redrawing, not a border move. The only 1177 land item on the Bohemond III page is the Harenc settlement ("renounced half of the nearby villages in favor of Bohemond", ledger gain at confidence 2). Antioch "survived Saladin's assault on Jerusalem in 1187".

5.5 k km2 for 1188-1259: the Saone district is outside the shape (3 cells), matching Saone captured in July 1188. The Bohemond III page is harsher than the shape: Saladin "occupied almost the whole Principality of Antioch in the summer of 1188" (Latakia 22/23 July, Orontes fortresses in August, Bagras 26 September) and "Bohemond managed to retain only his capital and the port of St Symeon"; the shape keeps the Orontes valley and the Baghras cell, and 3 cells of the Amanus circle lost to Leo in 1204. What Antioch recovered after the truce of 1 October 1188 to 31 May 1189 is not on the pages opened (gap), so the long-run shape is kept as ok. The 1201-1219 war moved the prince and, in 1204, the Amanus fortresses; Leo held Antioch 1216-1219 (occupation).

Cliopatria runs the 5.6 k km2 shape to 1271, but the principality ended in 1268: "Antioch fell on 18 May 1268" and the citadel two days later; the page does not say what remained afterwards. Draw 1260-1268 only; the dissolve event hands the land to the Mamluks. From 1260 Bohemond VI was a Mongol tributary (infobox "Vassal of the Ilkhanate (1260-1268)"). ledger.note: 1098-1099: Bohemond takes the surroundings. "took full control of Antioch as well as of the surrounding places such as Artah" and the harbour of St Symeon; the page dates this only "after the First Crusade". Cliopatria's 1099 shape is the result.

ledger.note: 1100-1112: Tancred's regency enlarges the principality; Cliopatria enlarges the shape in 1111. "Tancred expanded the borders of the Principality, seizing the cities of Tarsus and Latakia from the Byzantine Empire" - but these are not in Cliopatria's shape and the page dates neither. Tancred page (re-read 2026-10-25): Latakia taken in April or May 1103 after an 18-month siege and held again by 1108; Cilicia (Mamistra, Adana, Tarsus) lost after Harran (1104), campaigned 1106-1107, and "between 1109 and 1111 he finally conquered the whole of Cilicia"; the page does not mention Atharib in 1110-1111 and has Ridwan of Aleppo seize "Maarat, Albara, and Sarmin" after Harran in 1104, so Sarmin and Ma'arrat were Antiochene before 1104 and the 1111 step probably restores them. The dated step stays Cliopatria's (confidence 1); Latakia and Cilicia stay outside the keyframes (gap).

ledger.note: 1119: Baldwin II recovers the lost places after winning at Hab on 14 August. Hab page: "Baldwin managed to re-take all of the castles conquered by Ilghazi and prevented him from marching on Antioch" and, in the aftermath, "without opposition, Baldwin was able to recapture some of the places lost"; the Ager Sanguinis page says "Subsequently, Baldwin recovered some of the lost towns". Neither page names a town or a year beyond 1119; Zardana is only a hoped-for target (Robert Fulcoy "rode off ... to look into the possibility of retaking his stronghold of Zardana"). The five towns are returned together at confidence 1 because Cliopatria's shape keeps them to 1168; the circles replace the former union of Idlib province and Aleppo.

"Much of the eastern part of the Principality was lost, and Raymond was killed at the battle of Inab in 1149" (Principality page); "he was content with capturing all Antiochene territory east of the Orontes" (Nur ad-Din page); after the battle he "went on to capture the fortresses of Artah, Harim, and 'Imm" and the castle of Harim "fell to Muslim forces in 1149" (Harem, Syria page). The region is the 1152 shape minus the 1169 shape plus the Harim district: the 1169 shape still contains Harim (gazetteer check). Reviewer fix amended: the review asked to keep Harim out of this loss, but the Inab and Harem pages put Harim's fall in 1149, its retaking in 1158 and its final loss in 1164.

The Battle of Inab page says "Harim was not recovered until 1157"; the Harem page's 1158 is used because it names the actor. The district is a 10 km circle on the castle.

ledger.note: 1164: Nur ad-Din wins at Harim (12 August) and takes the fortress. "Nur ad-Din resumed the siege and captured Harim a few days later"; Bohemond III was captured; the Principality page adds that "the Orontes River became the permanent boundary between Antioch and Aleppo". Narrowed after review: only Harim and its district; the rest of the east bank went in 1149. Antioch itself was spared because the principality was "technically an Imperial fief".

region.text: "half of the nearby villages" of Harenc (Harim)

The page gives the year (the siege began "in December") and no list of villages; the 15 km circle is my reading. The gain is below the grid's resolution and does not explain Cliopatria's 1177 shape step (0 cells differ from 1169).

ledger.note: 1188: Saladin takes Saone. Bohemond III page: "His troops captured Latakia on 22 or 23 July, Sahyun six days later" (28 or 29 July); Principality page: "Saone was captured by Saladin from the last lord, Matthew, in 1188."

region.text: the part of the 1177 shape outside the 1188 shape

ledger.note: 1188: Saladin overruns the rest of the principality in the summer. Bohemond III page: "Saladin occupied almost the whole Principality of Antioch in the summer of 1188"; "the fortresses along the Orontes River in August"; Bagras surrendered "on 26 September"; the truce ran "from 1 October 1188 to 31 May 1189"; "Bohemond managed to retain only his capital and the port of St Symeon"; the Armengarde letter also lists Darbsak, Jabala and Burzey. The region stays Cliopatria's step (1177 shape minus 1188 shape, about 2.5 k km2): Latakia and Jabala were never in the shapes, Baghras is in both, and the 1188 shape keeps far more than the page says Bohemond retained; what Antioch won back after the truce is not on the pages opened (gap).

region.text: Antioch, claimed by Raymond-Roupen with Armenian backing

ledger.note: 1203: Leo II of Cilician Armenia enters Antioch (11 November) in the War of the Antiochene Succession but "failed to capture the citadel, which was held by the Templars and communal forces"; "Az-Zahir Ghazi soon invaded Cilician Armenia again, forcing Leo to withdraw from Antioch." He had besieged Antioch in 1201 for Raymond-Roupen against Bohemond IV, who "took Antioch without resistance" in April 1201.

1204: Leo has withdrawn from Antioch. The page says only that Ghazi's invasion forced him to withdraw "soon" after 11 November 1203 and gives no date; 1204 is a bridge. The contest is kept for this short entry; the later war is recorded as a loss (the Amanus fortresses, 1204) and an occupation (1216-1219) after review.

region.text: the Amanus Mountains (the same circle as the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia dossier's 1204 gain)

ledger.note: 1204: Leo seizes the Antiochene fortresses of the Amanus. "Exploiting the turmoil, Leo seized Antiochene fortresses in the Amanus Mountains, taking control of the route to Antioch." The page names no castle and no year of its own; it follows Renoart's rebellion of 1204 ("That same year"), which is the Armenian dossier's 1204 gain. The review said c. 1205: the only 1205 item on the page is the failed siege of Trapessac on 25 December 1205.

1216: Leo occupies Antioch for Raymond-Roupen. "Leo and his army entered Antioch during the night of 14 February 1216"; "Within days, the Templars, who held the citadel, surrendered without resistance"; "Raymond-Roupen was consecrated prince by the new Latin patriarch, Peter of Ivrea". Bohemond IV was absent. Recorded by the owner with the occupier as counterpart, as the Armenian dossier records it.
1219: a revolt led by William Farabel invites Bohemond IV back; Raymond-Roupen "fled to Cilicia after ceding the citadel to the Hospitallers" and "never regained Antioch"; Leo died in May 1219.
1268: Antioch falls to Baibars on 18 May. "Antioch fell on 18 May 1268"; "The citadel fell two days later"; "For three days Antioch was sacked".
1268: the principality ends. Infobox "Dissolved: 1268, when the Mamluk Sultanate under Baibars conquered it"; "He took the city in 1268, and northern Syria was quickly lost".

wars.outcome: Bohemond IV of Tripoli took Antioch in April 1201; Leo II of Armenia backed Raymond-Roupen, entered Antioch on 11 November 1203 (withdrew soon after), seized the Antiochene fortresses of the Amanus in 1204, held Antioch from 14 February 1216 and was beaten in 1219 when a revolt restored Bohemond IV; the war "came to a rather unspectacular end".
wars.note: Recorded after review as a short contest (1203/11-1204), a loss (the Amanus fortresses, 1204) and an occupation (Antioch, 1216/2-1219), as the Armenian dossier does for the last two; Leo lost Armenian forts north of the Taurus to the Seljuks while he was in Antioch. wars.name: Mongol and Mamluk conquest of Antioch
wars.outcome: Bohemond VI submitted to Hülegü in 1260 and Antioch became a Mongol tributary; after Ain Jalut Baibars "took the city in 1268"; Antioch fell on 18 May 1268 after a "relatively feeble defense".
wars.note: The Principality page: "Bohemond VI submitted to Hülegü ... Antioch became a tributary state of the Mongol Empire".

certainty.note: Frontiers with Aleppo and Byzantine Cilicia were never surveyed.

The Orontes was the frontier with Aleppo from the loss of the east bank in 1149 (Harim held again 1158-1164) and "the permanent boundary" after 1164, but the pages give no treaty line; the rest stays approximate.

notes: Principality of Antioch. Five pages opened (budget 5). Cliopatria begins in 1099 (the principality dates from 1098: new keyframe) and ends in 1271 (the principality fell on 18 May 1268; the pages say nothing about what stood after). Cliopatria never includes Latakia or Tarsus although the Principality page says Tancred "seiz[ed] the cities of Tarsus and Latakia from the Byzantine Empire" (undated; "lost after the Battle of Harran" in the page's words); the Battle of Harran and Treaty of Devol pages were not opened (budget). The pages do not give the 1108 terms. The shape step of 1169 (Cliopatria) is, after the 2026-10-25 repair, the 1149 loss of the east bank (Inab) with Harim lost in 1149, retaken in 1158 and lost in 1164 (ledger). The 1177 step is a redrawing (0 cells differ) and the 1188 step is explained by the Bohemond III page (summer 1188). VASSALAGE for other dossiers to carry (the suzerain records vassal_start/vassal_end): Byzantine Empire over Antioch 1138-1153 and 1159-1183 (infobox); Jerusalem over Antioch from 1119, "Antioch then became a vassal of Jerusalem, with Baldwin II as regent until 1126" (the Kingdom of Jerusalem dossier carries it); the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia 1254-1260; the Ilkhanate 1260-1268 (infobox; Bohemond VI submitted to Hülegü in 1260). Personal union: Bohemond IV was Count of Tripoli (from 1189) and Prince of Antioch (1201-1216, 1219-1233); Bohemonds V and VI also held both (County of Tripoli page). Tripoli's infobox lists the county as a vassal of Antioch and Jerusalem and the Mongols. Counterparts needing dossiers: artuqids (Ilghazi, 1119). Gazetteer names needed: Saône (Sahyun; coordinates used), Atharib, Zerdana, Sarmin, Ma'arrat al-Numan, Kafr Tab (Idlib province and west Aleppo are used). REPAIR 2026-10-25 (after review me-09-c). Applied: (1) 1149 loss of the east bank after Inab, mirrored by the Zengid dossier; (2) the 1164 loss narrowed to Harim, with Harim's fall in 1149 and retaking in 1158 added (Harem, Syria and Battle of Inab pages) and the keyframes 1139, 1152, 1169 marked adjust plus a new keyframe 1158-1163; (3) the 1119 loss and regain re-drawn as five 10 km circles on Atharib, Zerdana, Sarmin, Ma'arrat al-Numan and Kafr Tab (the Aleppo circle and all Idlib are gone; the regain is the same towns at confidence 1 because the Hab and Ager Sanguinis pages name none); (4) the Amanus castles lost to Cilicia in 1204 and the occupation of Antioch 1216/2-1219 (the contest is kept only for 1203/11-1204); (5) the 1188 step now rests on the Bohemond III page; (6) a 1177 gain of half the villages near Harim. NOT APPLIED: vassal_start/vassal_end pairs on this ledger. The schema (events.type) says a vassal event's 'counterpart' is the vassal itself in both events and the suzerain records it; written here with Jerusalem, Byzantium, Cilicia or the Mongols as counterpart, each pair would read as that state being Antioch's vassal.
